transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah, hi. I guess what made me come in is... I just keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody. Like, I'm totally a fake in my apprenticeship, you know? I'm supposed to be learning to fit pipes, but I feel like I've let my family down, and the younger apprentices, too, over stuff that... well, I know other people would probably just fix it and move on. But it's like, my uncle is a steamfitter, and he always used to tell these stories about how you have to be so precise, and one time he was working on this huge industrial boiler down at the old factory—they tore that place down last year, actually, to build those ugly new condos, which is a shame because the brickwork was really something. I always liked looking at the old brickwork when I drove past. But anyway, yeah, I just feel like I'm letting everyone down and I can't shake it.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like looking at brickwork or anything else?

Yeah, I guess so. It's like... lately, I can just walk right past my sketchbook, which is weird for me. And I've been skipping volleyball, ignoring all the texts from my volunteer group. I just don't feel much of anything about it, even though those used to be the things that, you know, made me feel like myself. It's kind of like how they stopped running the local bus route down my street. I used to take that bus all the time when I was little to go to the library. The library had this amazing section on local history, and I'd just sit there for hours looking at old maps of the city. The maps showed all the old streetcar lines that don't exist anymore. It's crazy how much the city has changed, you know? Like, they just pave over everything. But yeah, I just don't really care about my sketchbook or volleyball right now.
Have you noticed that you're feeling more tired or that you're lacking energy, even if you're not doing much? Like, does just getting through the day feel heavier than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. Like, my energy is fine, I don't feel physically heavy or tired or anything like that. I still get up at my normal time and have my coffee... actually, I had to get a new thermos for work recently because my old one got run over. It rolled right off the tailgate at the job site. We're doing some piping for this commercial HVAC install right now, and the site is just a total mess. There are pallets of drywall everywhere, and the drywall guys are always leaving their dust all over our fittings. It's so annoying because then you have to wipe everything down before you can even prep the joint. My dad used to say that drywallers are the messiest people in construction, and I'm starting to think he's right. He used to build custom cabinets, so he was super neat about everything. He had this whole vacuum system set up for his sawdust in the garage, which was pretty loud, but it kept the floor spotless. But yeah, anyway, I'm not really lacking energy or feeling weighed down.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you've let people down more than usual, even if it's over small things?

Yeah, I mean... I think I said that earlier, right? About feeling like I ruined things for everybody? It's just... I'm a total fake in my apprenticeship. I feel like I've completely let my family down, and even the younger apprentices. And it's over stuff that... well, I know other people would probably just fix the mistake and move on. But it just sticks with me. It's kind of like when you get a bad weld, you know? Like, if the temperature isn't exactly right, the metal just doesn't fuse properly, and you can't always see it from the outside. You have to use this special dye penetrant to check for cracks, which is this bright red liquid that gets everywhere if you aren't careful. I got it on my favorite work shirt once, the one with the flannel lining. I bought that shirt at this surplus store that used to be downtown, right next to the old diner that made those huge milkshakes. They had a strawberry one that was just... amazing. I think the owner retired and moved to Florida, though. But yeah, I just feel like I'm letting everyone down and I can't let it go.

Can you tell me more about how you feel when you think about things you used to enjoy, like sketching or looking at old maps? Do they bring you any pleasure anymore, or do they feel completely uninteresting to you?

I think I mentioned this a little bit ago, but yeah, it's just... I can walk right past my sketchbook now. And I skip my volleyball games, I just ignore all the texts from my volunteer group. I don't feel much of anything about any of it anymore, which sucks because those were the things that made me feel like myself, you know? It's kind of like how when you have a favorite tool and it just stops working right. I had this pipe wrench that I loved, it was a 14-inch Ridgid, aluminum so it was lighter. I bought it when I first started my apprenticeship. I actually got it at this hardware store out by the highway, the one with the huge neon sign shaped like a hammer. The sign is actually broken right now, only the handle lights up. It's been like that since that big storm we had last month. The wind was so crazy, it blew our neighbor's trash cans all the way down the street. We had to go hunting for them the next morning in the rain. But yeah, I just... I don't get any pleasure out of the stuff I used to like. It's all just blank.
Have you been having trouble focusing or making decisions lately, even about small things?

Um, no, I don't think so. My focus is pretty normal, and making decisions hasn't really been an issue. Like, I just had to pick out a new pair of work boots yesterday because my old steel toes were wearing completely thin on the heel, and it was pretty easy to choose. I ended up deciding on these Timberland Pros because they have this anti-fatigue matting built right into the sole. I bought them at that big shoe warehouse over by the mall, the one that actually used to be a roller rink back in the day. My mom always talks about it because she actually met my dad at that roller rink during a couples skate. I think they were playing some Journey song, or maybe it was Foreigner? I don't know, but she still has her old skates in a box in our basement. They're this retro white leather with these bright pink wheels. They're sitting right next to our water heater, which reminds me, the water heater actually needs a new thermocouple. It's been acting up, the pilot light keeps going out, so I should probably look at that this weekend since I have the tools for it anyway from work. But, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, decisions and focusing. Yeah, no, I haven't had any trouble with that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in response to specific things?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I haven't really been feeling sad or down all day, every day. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, like when we're on a job and the general contractor messes up the timeline. Like last week, we were supposed to be roughing in the pipes for this new house, but the framing wasn't even done yet. It's super annoying because you just end up standing around. My foreman gets so mad when that happens. He drives this huge Ford F-250, and he just sat in the cab listening to sports radio for like two hours. He listens to that station that does the really aggressive trivia contests in the morning. I actually called in once and won a pair of tickets to a minor league baseball game. The seats were right behind home plate, which was cool, but the hot dogs there were so overpriced. I think they charged like eight bucks for a plain hot dog, and they didn't even have the good mustard, just those little yellow packets that are always impossible to tear open if your hands are even a little bit sweaty. I always keep a pocket knife on me for stuff like that, just a little Swiss Army one my grandpa gave me. It has the little tweezers in it that I always lose. But yeah, anyway... no, I don't feel depressed all day. Just normal, I guess.
Have you been feeling guilty about things more than usual, or like you're worthless or a failure, even when it doesn't make sense?

Yeah, actually. That's... that's kind of the main reason I even came in to see you. I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm this huge fake in my apprenticeship, and I'm letting my family down, and the younger apprentices too. And it's over stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, but it just eats at me. Speaking of the younger apprentices, there's this one guy, Tommy, who just started. He's always dropping his tools down the shafts. I swear, last week he dropped his tape measure down three floors. It was one of those really nice Stanley FatMax ones too, the ones with the 11-foot standout. I actually have the exact same tape measure, but I keep mine on a lanyard now because I lost one in a crawl space a couple of years ago. That crawl space was so gross, it was full of these weird camel crickets. Have you ever seen those? They look like spiders but they jump right at you. I had to army-crawl through this tiny gap just to get to the main water shutoff, and I was covered in cobwebs by the time I got out. My coveralls were completely ruined. I usually buy the Carhartt ones, the insulated ones for winter, because it gets freezing on the rough-in sites when there aren't any windows installed yet. But yeah, anyway, I just... I feel like a complete failure a lot of the time, and I feel so guilty about it.
Can you tell me if there have been days when you don’t feel any pleasure or interest in most activities, even things you used to really enjoy, like sketching or looking at old maps?

Yeah, actually, that's been happening a lot. Lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, or skip my volleyball games, and I just ignore the volunteer group texts without feeling much of anything. And those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? Especially volleyball. I used to play setter, which is like being the quarterback of the team. You have to call the plays and know where everyone is. We played in this rec league at the community center downtown. The gym there has this weird squeaky floor that always sounds like a flock of birds when everyone is running around. They actually just refinished it last summer, but they used this really cheap sealant, so it scuffed up almost immediately. I know a guy who does flooring, he's a subcontractor we work with sometimes, named Dave. Dave has this massive beard, like ZZ Top level, and he always wears these bright neon orange suspenders. He said he wears them so he doesn't get run over by the forklift guys at the supply yard. Those forklift guys are crazy, they whip around corners so fast. One time I saw a guy drop an entire pallet of PVC fittings. It sounded like a giant box of Lego exploding. We use PVC for the drain lines, mostly Schedule 40, which is the thick white pipe. You have to use this purple primer before you glue it, and the primer stains everything. I have it all over my hands right now, actually. It takes days to wash off, even with pumice soap. But um, yeah, I just don't care about my sketching or volleyball or any of that stuff right now.
Have you had days where you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just every once in a while or in response to something that happened?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? I'm pretty sure I said no, I don't feel sad all day. I mean, I get frustrated, like I was saying about the job site and the framing being behind. It's just so disorganized sometimes. Our project manager, Steve, he's always losing the blueprints. He actually left them on the roof of his truck once and drove off, and they flew everywhere down the highway. We had to use the digital copies on his iPad, but the screen on his iPad is completely shattered. It looks like a spiderweb. He dropped it when he was trying to carry three coffees and a box of donuts at the same time. They were from this place called Donut King, which is open 24 hours. They have these massive apple fritters, like the size of a dinner plate. I can never finish one by myself. My dog usually gets the rest. He's a pitbull mix named Buster, and he loves anything sweet, which I know is bad for him, but he gives you those puppy dog eyes. He has one blue eye and one brown eye. I think it's called heterochromia. I read about it on Wikipedia once when I couldn't sleep. I end up reading the most random stuff on there. Last night I read an entire article about the history of the stapler. Did you know the first stapler was made for King Louis XV of France? Every staple had his royal seal on it. It's crazy what people used to spend money on. But anyway... yeah, I'm pretty sure I already answered that. I don't feel depressed all day long.
Have you had days where you feel like nothing really interests you or brings you pleasure, even things you used to enjoy, and does that last for most of the day, nearly every day?

Wait, didn't we just talk about this too? I feel like we're going in circles a bit here. But yeah, like I said before, I just... I don't really care about the stuff I usually like. Lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, or skip my volleyball games, and I just ignore the volunteer group texts without feeling much of anything. And those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? The volunteer group is actually for this animal shelter on the east side of town. We mostly just walk the dogs and clean out the kennels. The kennels smell so strongly of bleach, it kind of burns your nose when you first walk in. They buy it in these massive 55-gallon drums. I know a lot about drums like that because we use similar ones on the big commercial plumbing jobs for storing excess primer and solvent. You have to be really careful with those solvents, they're super flammable. One time this guy on a site in the city was smoking too close to the storage area and caused a flash fire. The fire department had to come and everything. The fire trucks here are painted this really bright yellow-green color instead of red. I read somewhere that human eyes see that color better at night or something. It's called optic yellow, I think. Same color as tennis balls. I used to play tennis when I was a kid, but I was terrible at it. I could never get the serve right. You have to throw the ball up so high and then time the swing perfectly. It's way harder than setting a volleyball, honestly. But um, yeah... I'm pretty sure I already told you that I've been losing interest in everything. It's been happening a lot lately.
Have you felt like nothing really interests you or brings you pleasure — even things you used to enjoy — for most of the day, nearly every day, not just sometimes or for a short while?

Are you... are you messing with me right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. You literally just asked me this exact same question, like, three times in a row. Didn't I just say yes? Yes, I've been completely blowing off my sketching, my volleyball games, the animal shelter... all of it. None of it sounds fun right now. It's like someone just flipped a switch and I don't care anymore. Which is weird because I usually care a lot, especially about the animal shelter. 

We actually had this one dog there, a mastiff mix, who weighed almost as much as I do. His name was Tank. He was so big he couldn't even fit in the regular kennels, they had to put him in the quarantine room just because it had more floor space. The quarantine room always has this weird hum to it because of the ventilation system. It's a negative pressure room, so it pulls the air out so diseases don't spread. We install systems like that sometimes in hospitals. The ductwork for those is massive, like you could crawl through it like in the movies. Die Hard is always the first movie I think of when I see big air ducts. Bruce Willis crawling around with a lighter. My dad used to watch that movie every Christmas. He insisted it was a Christmas movie. We'd always order Chinese food and watch Die Hard. The Chinese place we ordered from had the best crab rangoons, they actually put real crab in them, not just that imitation stuff that looks like pink string cheese. I hate string cheese. It always squeaks against your teeth when you bite it. 

But seriously, doc, are you reading off a script or something? Because I'm pretty sure I've told you three times now that I have zero interest in doing anything I usually like doing. It's an all-day, every-day kind of thing right now.
Can you clarify whether you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific situations?

Okay, seriously, is there an echo in here? I really feel like you're just asking me the same two questions over and over again. I already told you, no, I don't feel sad all day. I get annoyed, like with Steve and his shattered iPad, but I'm not sitting around crying or feeling depressed all day. I mean, maybe I'm just tired. I've been working a lot of overtime lately because we're trying to finish up the rough-in on this new apartment complex downtown. It's a huge job, like six stories. We have to run all the main water lines up through the central chases. It's exhausting work, mostly because you have to lug these massive lengths of copper pipe up the stairs since the elevators aren't installed yet. Copper is so expensive right now, too. We had a guy try to steal a bunch of it off the site last week. He backed his pickup truck right up to the fence at like 2 AM. The security guard caught him, though. The guard is this older guy, always wears a high-vis vest that's way too big for him. It looks like he's wearing a neon tent. He told me he used to be a roadie for some 80s hair metal band. I can't remember which one... maybe Whitesnake? Or Def Leppard? I love that song "Pour Some Sugar On Me." It always gets stuck in my head. I heard it at the grocery store the other day when I was trying to decide between smooth or chunky peanut butter. I always go with chunky, it has more texture. Smooth is just... boring. Kinda like how this conversation feels right now, no offense. But yeah, for the millionth time, I am not depressed or down all day. I'm just not into doing anything right now.
Can you clarify whether you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific situations?

Are you... is this a joke? Because I swear you just asked me that exact same thing. Like, word for word. I feel like I'm stuck in Groundhog Day. Do you know that movie? With Bill Murray? He wakes up every day at 6:00 AM to that Sonny and Cher song, "I Got You Babe." My mom used to listen to them all the time. She had this huge collection of vinyl records in the basement. The basement always smelled like damp cardboard and mothballs, probably because of all the old clothes she kept down there. She had this one leather jacket from the 70s with fringe all down the sleeves. I tried to wear it for Halloween once when I went as a biker, but it was way too big. I ended up looking more like a bat. We went to this haunted house that year, the kind where they have actors jump out at you in the dark. I accidentally punched one of the actors in the face because he scared me so bad. I felt terrible, but it was a total reflex. Reflexes are weird, right? Like when the doctor hits your knee with that little rubber hammer. 

But anyway, no, I am not depressed most of the day. I'm not sitting around crying. I'm just... existing, I guess. But seriously, are you writing this down? Because I really don't want to answer this again.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly or concentrating on tasks lately, even ones that you normally find straightforward?

No, I wouldn't say I'm having trouble thinking clearly. I mean, my brain works fine. I can still do my job, which takes a lot of concentration, you know? Like, when you're measuring pipe, you have to be exact. If you're off by even a quarter of an inch, the whole run is messed up and you have to start over. Copper isn't cheap. My boss, Frank, he gets so mad when we waste material. He turns this bright shade of purple, almost like an eggplant. Have you ever tried to grow eggplants? I tried starting a garden last spring, but the rabbits ate everything. They got right through the chicken wire I put up. Rabbits are surprisingly smart. Or maybe I'm just bad at building fences. I should stick to plumbing. But yeah, no problems concentrating, really. I can focus just fine when I need to.
Have you had any trouble thinking clearly or concentrating on tasks lately, even ones you normally find straightforward?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Seriously, I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. Are you reading off a script or something? Because I literally just said my concentration is fine. My brain works perfectly well. I don't know why you keep repeating yourself. It's like my dog, Buster. He's a golden retriever mix, and he will literally fetch a tennis ball until he drops. You throw it, he brings it back, you throw it, he brings it back. Over and over and over. One time we were at the park for three hours just doing that. He finally just laid down in the dirt, panting like crazy. He had this goofy smile on his face, though, with his tongue hanging out the side. Dogs are so pure, you know? They don't overcomplicate things. They just want to play and eat and sleep. I wish life was that simple. But yeah, no, I'm not having any trouble thinking or focusing. I'm totally fine on that front.
Have you had days where you feel like nothing really interests you or brings you pleasure, even things you used to enjoy, and does that last for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I guess so. Like, lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook and not even care. I used to draw all the time, mostly like, architectural stuff or pipe layouts, just for fun. And I've been skipping my volleyball games, too. I just ignore the group texts from my volunteer group without feeling much of anything, even though those used to be the things that made me feel like myself. It's weird. Speaking of volleyball, did you see the Olympics this year? The indoor teams are insane, but beach volleyball is where it's really at. I don't know how they jump like that in the sand. Have you ever tried running in dry sand? It's like a workout for muscles you didn't even know you had. My calves were screaming the last time I went to the beach. We went down to the coast last summer, me and a few friends, and we tried to build this massive sandcastle. Like, a fortress. We even dug a moat and tried to fill it with ocean water, but the sand just kept absorbing it. It's crazy how porous sand is. Kind of like a sponge. Sponges are actually animals, you know? Like, sea sponges. They just sit there on the ocean floor filtering water. Sounds kind of peaceful, honestly. Just floating there, not having to worry about anything. But yeah, to answer your question, I just haven't been interested in much lately.
Have you had days where you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just occasionally or in response to specific things?

Not really, no. I don't feel depressed or down all day. I mean, I spend a lot of my day literally *down* in crawlspaces and basements for work, but that's just plumbing for you. You wouldn't believe the stuff people leave under their houses, by the way. Just last Tuesday I was fixing a leaky PVC joint under this old Victorian place, and I found a whole box of those antique glass medicine bottles. Like, the really old ones that are tinted deep blue and green? My grandma actually used to collect blue glass. She had this big bay window in her kitchen and she’d line them all up on the sill. When the afternoon sun came through, it made the whole kitchen look like you were underwater. She used to bake sourdough bread in that kitchen all the time. Sourdough is so much work, you know? You have to feed the starter every single day or it dies. It's basically a very demanding, sticky pet. I tried keeping a starter alive once, but I totally forgot about it over a long weekend and it smelled like a warm brewery by the time I remembered. So gross. But yeah, anyway, no, I don't feel depressed like that.
Can you clarify whether you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally or in response to specific situations?

I literally just said no. Like, wait, didn't you just ask me that exact same thing? I feel like we're going in circles here. I told you, I don't feel depressed. I'm not sitting around feeling down all day. I mean, sure, sometimes I get annoyed, like when I'm trying to explain something and people don't listen. That happens a lot at work. You'd think people would listen to the plumber when their basement is flooding, but no, they always want to argue about the cost of copper piping versus PEX. PEX is so much easier to work with, honestly. You just crimp it and you're done. Copper is a whole thing with the blowtorch and the solder. Have you ever used a blowtorch? It's kind of satisfying, honestly. Just melting the metal and watching it seal the joint perfectly. You have to be careful, though, or you'll scorch the floor joists. My boss, Frank, he scorched a whole beam once and the homeowner freaked out. Frank's a good guy, though. He always brings donuts on Fridays. Maple bars are the best, don't you think? But yeah, no, I'm not depressed. We just went over this.
Do you feel more down or depressed in the morning when you first wake up compared to other times of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel worse in the morning. Honestly, mornings are usually pretty okay for me. I mean, getting out of bed can be tough, especially when it's cold. You know how it is when you just want to stay under the covers? My apartment gets so drafty in the winter. I think the seals around the windows are completely shot. I've been meaning to re-caulk them, but I just haven't gotten around to it. Caulking is actually kind of an art form. If you don't do it in one smooth motion, it looks all clumpy and terrible. You have to wet your finger just right to smooth it out. Some guys use soapy water, but I think just plain spit works best, honestly. It's a trick an old timer taught me when I was an apprentice. He was a character, that guy. Always wore these bright red suspenders, even under his coveralls. He said they kept his pants up better when he was crawling under sinks. Sinks are the worst, especially the pedestal ones. There's zero room to maneuver a wrench behind them. You practically have to be a contortionist. I pulled a muscle in my neck once trying to tighten a slip nut on a pedestal sink. Had to wear one of those foam collars for a week. So embarrassing. But yeah, no, mornings aren't really any worse than the rest of the day for me.
